title: Over 1.5 Million Pounds of Meat Recalled After Warehouse Cooling Fault
summaryZh: 美國Kayem食品因倉庫冷卻故障，全國召回逾150萬磅肉品。
summaryHi: गोदाम की कूलिंग खराब होने से अमेरिका में 15 लाख पाउंड से ज़्यादा मांस वापस मंगाया गया।
summaryEs: Una avería de refrigeración obliga a retirar más de 1,5 millones de libras de carne en EE. UU.
summaryJa: 倉庫の冷却故障で、米国で150万ポンド超の食肉製品が全国回収に。
summaryKo: 창고 냉각 장치 고장으로 미국에서 150만 파운드 넘는 육류가 리콜됐다.
summaryEn: A US meat company is recalling more than 1.5 million pounds of hot dogs, bacon and other meat because a warehouse cooling system failed.
paragraphs: Kayem Foods, a meat producer based in Chelsea, Massachusetts, is recalling more than 1.5 million pounds of ready-to-eat meat and poultry products sold across the United States, the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) announced.

The company said it had recently found a malfunction in the cooling system at one of its warehouses. According to the USDA, the products 'may have experienced temperature abuse during storage', meaning they may not have been kept cold enough to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria.

The list of affected items is long. It includes hot dogs, among them the well-known 'Fenway Franks' sold at Boston's baseball stadium, as well as bacon, bologna, kielbasa, bratwurst, ham, corned beef, chicken sausage and turkey breast. All were stored and shipped to retailers and food service outlets nationwide between June 7 and October 14.

No illnesses linked to the products have been reported. Even so, officials fear that some of the food may still be sitting in home refrigerators, and they advise anyone who finds it to throw it away. Affected packages carry one of three establishment numbers inside the USDA inspection mark.

Chief executive Matt Monkiewicz said the firm was acting 'out of an abundance of caution' and that management took full responsibility. It is not Kayem's first recall: last year it withdrew more than 24,000 pounds of chicken sausage that may have contained pieces of plastic.
A big meat company in the United States is asking people to throw away some of its food. The company is called Kayem Foods. It is near Boston.
The food includes hot dogs, bacon, ham, sausages and chicken. In total, it weighs more than 1.5 million pounds. That is about 700,000 kilograms.
Why? The company found a problem in one of its buildings. The machine that keeps food cold broke. Meat must stay cold. If it gets warm, it may not be safe to eat.
The food went to shops and restaurants all over the country between June and October. So far, nobody has become ill.
The government says people should look in their fridges. If they have this food, they should throw it away. The company's boss said, 'We take full responsibility.'

A food company in Massachusetts is recalling more than 1.5 million pounds of ready-to-eat meat and chicken products across the United States. The US Department of Agriculture (USDA) announced the recall over the weekend.

Kayem Foods says it recently discovered that the cooling system at one of its warehouses was not working properly. This means the food may have become too warm while it was stored, which can allow harmful bacteria to grow.

The recall covers many popular products, including hot dogs such as 'Fenway Franks', bacon, ham, bologna, sausages, corned beef and turkey breast. They were stored and sent to shops and restaurants nationwide between June 7 and October 14.

No one has reported getting sick so far. However, the USDA is worried that some of the products may still be in people's fridges at home. It says anyone who has them should throw them away and not eat them.
Shoppers can check a special number on the package to see if their food is affected. The company's chief executive said the recall was voluntary and that the company takes full responsibility.

Kayem Foods, a meat producer based in Chelsea, Massachusetts, is recalling more than 1.5 million pounds of ready-to-eat meat and poultry products sold across the United States, the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) announced.

The company said it had recently found a malfunction in the cooling system at one of its warehouses. According to the USDA, the products 'may have experienced temperature abuse during storage', meaning they may not have been kept cold enough to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria.

The list of affected items is long. It includes hot dogs, among them the well-known 'Fenway Franks' sold at Boston's baseball stadium, as well as bacon, bologna, kielbasa, bratwurst, ham, corned beef, chicken sausage and turkey breast. All were stored and shipped to retailers and food service outlets nationwide between June 7 and October 14.

No illnesses linked to the products have been reported. Even so, officials fear that some of the food may still be sitting in home refrigerators, and they advise anyone who finds it to throw it away. Affected packages carry one of three establishment numbers inside the USDA inspection mark.

Chief executive Matt Monkiewicz said the firm was acting 'out of an abundance of caution' and that management took full responsibility. It is not Kayem's first recall: last year it withdrew more than 24,000 pounds of chicken sausage that may have contained pieces of plastic.

A Massachusetts meat processor has launched one of the largest food recalls of the year, pulling more than 1.5 million pounds of ready-to-eat meat and poultry from shelves nationwide after a refrigeration failure at one of its warehouses.

Kayem Foods, headquartered in Chelsea, just outside Boston, told federal regulators it had recently identified a cooling system malfunction. The US Department of Agriculture said the products 'may have experienced temperature abuse during storage', a technical phrase indicating that they could have spent time above the temperatures needed to keep bacteria in check.

The sweep is remarkably broad, encompassing hot dogs, including the 'Fenway Franks' synonymous with Boston's ballpark, alongside bacon, bologna, kielbasa, bratwurst, brisket, ham, liverwurst and turkey breast. The goods were stored and dispatched to retailers and food service operators across the country between June 7 and October 14.

No illnesses have been reported so far. The bigger concern for regulators is that items may linger in household fridges, and consumers are being urged to discard rather than eat anything bearing the relevant establishment numbers.

Chief executive Matt Monkiewicz described the move as voluntary, taken 'out of an abundance of caution', and said management accepted full responsibility. The episode follows a far smaller recall last year, when Kayem withdrew more than 24,000 pounds of chicken sausage over possible plastic contamination.

A meat company in the north-eastern United States has recalled more than 1.5 million pounds of ready-to-eat products after discovering a fault in a warehouse cooling system. The case illustrates how a single technical failure can affect food supplies across an entire country.

Kayem Foods, based near Boston, informed the US Department of Agriculture that refrigeration at one of its storage sites had malfunctioned. As a result, the products may have been exposed to unsafe temperatures, which can allow dangerous bacteria to multiply even in food that looks and smells normal.

The recall covers a wide range of items, including hot dogs, bacon, ham, sausages and turkey breast. These products were distributed to supermarkets, restaurants and other food service outlets nationwide over a period of more than four months.

Although no illnesses have been reported, the authorities are concerned that many consumers may still have the affected food at home. They have therefore advised the public to check packaging carefully and to discard any items identified in the recall rather than risk eating them.

The company's chief executive stressed that the decision was voluntary and that management accepted full responsibility. Food safety experts often argue that such prompt action, although costly, is essential for maintaining public trust in the food industry.

noteEs.usage: Se usa prompt action/response; adverbio promptly.

noteJa.exampleTr: 会社の迅速な対応が顧客を守った。
noteJa.usage: prompt action/response の形が多い。副詞 promptly。

properly.en: in the correct or right way
properly.ex: The heater is not working properly this morning.

public.ex: Public transport is cheap in the city.

pulling.ex: Horses were pulling a heavy cart.

range.ex: The shop sells a range of products.

rather.ex: I'd like tea rather than coffee.

ready-to-eat.ja: 調理済みの；そのまま食べられる
ready-to-eat.en: able to be eaten without cooking
ready-to-eat.ex: She bought a ready-to-eat salad for lunch.

recall.en: an order to return unsafe products
recall.ex: The car maker announced a recall of 10,000 vehicles.

recalled.en: asked buyers to return a faulty product
recalled.ex: The toys were recalled because of small loose parts.

recalling.en: asking buyers to return a faulty product
recalling.ex: The shop is recalling a brand of baby food.

recalls.ex: Food recalls have increased in recent years.

refrigeration.ex: Fresh fish needs good refrigeration during transport.

refrigerators.ex: Most homes in the area have modern refrigerators.

regulators.en: official bodies that control an industry
regulators.ex: Regulators fined the bank for poor service.

example.en: The energy regulator blocked the price rise.
example.zh: 能源監管機構阻止了這次漲價。

note.meaning: 負責監督某個產業、確保其遵守規則的官方機構。
note.usage: 常見 competition/energy/financial regulator；regulator 和 watchdog 在新聞中常互換。

noteHi.exampleTr: ऊर्जा नियामक ने मूल्य वृद्धि रोक दी।
noteHi.meaning: किसी उद्योग पर नज़र रखने वाली सरकारी संस्था।
noteHi.usage: financial/competition regulator आम हैं; समाचारों में watchdog भी कहा जाता है।

noteEs.exampleTr: El regulador energético bloqueó la subida de precios.
noteEs.meaning: organismo oficial que controla un sector.
noteEs.usage: Se usa financial/competition regulator; en prensa también watchdog.

noteJa.exampleTr: エネルギー規制当局は値上げを阻止した。
noteJa.meaning: ある産業を監督する公的機関。
noteJa.usage: financial / competition regulator など。報道では watchdog とも言う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 에너지 규제 기관이 가격 인상을 막았다.
noteKo.usage: financial/competition regulator 등으로 쓰인다. 뉴스에서는 watchdog과 자주 바꿔 쓴다.

noteEn.meaning: An official body that controls an industry.
noteEn.usage: Common in 'financial regulator'; news also uses 'watchdog'.

relevant.ex: Please bring all relevant documents to the meeting.

remarkably.en: in a surprising or unusual way

reported.ex: The theft was reported to the police.

responsibility.en: a duty or blame for something
responsibility.ex: The manager took responsibility for the mistake.

restaurants.en: places where you buy and eat meals
restaurants.ex: The new restaurants in town are very busy.

result.ex: Heavy rain can result in floods.

retailers.en: shops or companies that sell goods to people
retailers.ex: Many retailers offer discounts in January.

risk.en: the chance that something bad will happen
risk.ex: Smoking increases the risk of disease.

safe.ex: Keep your passport in a safe place.

safety.ex: Wear a helmet for your safety.

sausage.en: minced meat in a long skin
sausage.ex: He had a sausage and eggs for breakfast.

sausages.ex: We cooked sausages on the grill last night.

says.ex: Experts say the plan will work.

sent.ex: I sent the form to the office yesterday.

service.ex: The bus service runs every hour.

shelves.en: flat boards in shops for goods
shelves.ex: The shop's shelves were empty after the storm.

shipped.ex: The orders were shipped on Monday morning.

shoppers.en: people who buy things in shops
shoppers.ex: The mall was full of shoppers on Saturday.

shops.ex: The local shop closes at nine.

sick.ex: She stayed home because she was sick.

single.ex: He didn't say a single word.

sites.ex: There are two recycling sites in town.

sitting.ex: Old letters were sitting in a box for years.

smells.ex: The bread smells fresh and warm.

so.en: used in 'so far' meaning until now
so.ex: So far, everything is going well.

some.ex: Some fifty people came to the meeting.

special.ex: The area has a special feeling.

spent.ex: They spent too much on the party.

stadium.en: a large sports ground with seats

states.ex: EU member states agreed the plan.

stay.ex: Most tourists stay in the centre.

storage.ex: Energy storage helps when there is no sun.

stored.en: kept in a place for later use
stored.ex: The rice is stored in a cool, dry place.

stressed.en: said strongly that it is important
stressed.ex: She stressed the need for care.

supplies.en: amounts of something available to use

sweep.en: to move quickly over a large area
sweep.ex: Strong winds will sweep across the country.

synonymous.ex: The city is synonymous with great coffee.

system.en: a set of rules or ways of working

take.ex: Many parents will take a day off.

takes.en: in "takes over": fills or controls a place
takes.ex: Music takes over the square at night.

technical.en: related to machines or special methods
technical.ex: The flight was delayed by a technical problem.

temperature.en: how hot or cold something is

temperatures.ex: Temperatures dropped below zero last night.

therefore.ex: It was late; therefore, we took a taxi.

these.en: the ones here or just mentioned

time.ex: For the first time, dentists will join.

told.ex: She told me a funny story.

too.ex: The coffee is too hot to drink.

took.en: used in 'took part' meaning joined in
took.ex: Everyone took part in the game.

total.ex: The total cost was two million.

trust.en: belief that someone is honest and safe
trust.ex: Trust is hard to win back once lost.

turkey.en: a large bird eaten as meat
turkey.ex: We had turkey sandwiches for lunch.

united.zh: 美國（United States 的一部分）
united.en: part of the name United States; joined together
united.ex: The United States has fifty states.

unsafe.ex: The old bridge is unsafe for trucks.

urged.en: strongly asked someone to do something
urged.ex: The doctor urged him to stop smoking.

voluntary.en: done by choice, not by law
voluntary.ex: Joining the club is completely voluntary.

example.en: Taking part in the survey is completely voluntary.
example.zh: 參加調查完全出於自願。

note.usage: 常見 voluntary recall/work；on a voluntary basis；副詞 voluntarily。

noteEn.meaning: done by choice, not because you are forced.

noteHi.exampleTr: सर्वे में भाग लेना पूरी तरह स्वैच्छिक है।
noteHi.usage: voluntary recall; on a voluntary basis आम हैं।

noteEs.exampleTr: Participar en la encuesta es totalmente voluntario.
noteEs.usage: Se usa voluntary recall; on a voluntary basis.

noteJa.exampleTr: 調査への参加は完全に任意だ。
noteJa.meaning: 自発的な；強制ではない。
noteJa.usage: voluntary recall、on a voluntary basis の形が多い。

noteKo.usage: voluntary recall, on a voluntary basis 형태가 흔하다.

warehouse.en: a large building for storing goods
warehouse.ex: The goods are kept in a warehouse near the port.

warehouses.ex: The company owns three warehouses in Texas.

weekend.ex: We go hiking at the weekend.

weighs.en: weighs X against Y: compares to decide
weighs.ex: She weighs the cost against the benefits.

well.ex: She speaks Irish as well as English.

well-known.ex: The café is well-known for its cakes.

were.ex: The shops were closed on Sunday.

wide.en: measuring a certain distance from side to side
wide.ex: The river is fifty metres wide here.

withdrew.ex: The unions withdrew from the talks.

worried.ex: She is worried about her exam.
